interactions.summary: After another student's brief assent, a student links Dante's blinding brightness to Moses being overwhelmed by God and receiving the commandments, and Jiang explicitly accepts that prophetic reading.
A student reads Dante's theological answer that the highest love bends toward God because all other goods are only reflected rays of the supreme good.

Jiang compresses the reading into a recap that God is love, God is implanted in humans, and humans return to that love by loving others; the next reading then makes love an action that turns the heart from twisted love toward God, ending in heavenly acclamation.

claims.claim: Jiang accepts the student's comparison between Dante's dazzlement and Moses being blinded by God's presence, treating the episode as part of a prophetic pattern.
The reading frames God as the supreme good and all other goods as reflected rays, which is why the highest love properly aims at God.
Jiang summarizes the lesson as: God is love, God implanted himself in humans, and humans return to love by loving other people.
The reading and Jiang's gloss both treat love as the active force that pulls people out of twisted love and reorients the universe toward God.
claims.temporal_scope: Interpretive and textual claim stated on 2026-06-18.

signature_moments.moment: All finite goods become rays cast from one radiance, making love a movement back toward the source rather than attachment to fragments.
signature_moments.source_phrase: nothing but a ray reflected from its radiance
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is one of the packet's cleanest metaphysical images and gives later episode compression a memorable formulation.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang turns the theology into a simple circuit: God is love, humans carry that imprint, and loving others is the route back.
signature_moments.source_phrase: we aspire to return to love
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It condenses a long reading into a reusable Jiang-world-model sentence for the public read.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: A misdirected form of desire from which right love must pull the soul back toward God.
The highest object of love in Dante's argument, with all lesser goods treated as reflections of it.
